# SC.0 - General Security & Command Expectations Security and Command are held to higher standards of roleplay.
As a member of Security or Command, you have a greater effect on the enjoyment of other players and on the potential of the roundflow. You're expected to weigh your decisions accordingly and remember: You are not above being arrested for violating ISG.
# SC.1 - The Internal Security Guidelines Security, The CO, and the Captain have a higher degree of expectations towards upholding and maintaining the Internal Security Guidelines.
This does not mean they are fully beholden to the document, however they should aim to uphold the spirit of it as much as possible.
The Head of Security and the Warden have a higher degree of expectations towards knowing and understanding the ISG.
As it is an IC document, it may be ignored in emergency situations in service of performing your Role.
# SC.2 - Standard Operating Procedures Members of Command have a higher degree of expectation when it comes to understanding and utilizing the Standard Operating Procedures.
As it is an IC document, it may be ignored in emergency situations in service of performing your Role.
[color=#ffb74d]- ! We are still working on SOP ! -[/color]
# SC.3 Security & Command Fear and Bribery RP Command and Security are allowed to be engaged in Fear and Bribery RP, however they should be less coerceable and bribeable than regular crew.
As Bribery is a crime under the ISG, Security should not be bribed lightly, and they should not give up any weapons or armour. Members of Security should be able to feel like they can trust each other.
Command and Security should not bribe or coerce. This does not include bargaining. - Bribery and coercion is the act of using the promise of material gain (such as wealth) or the threat of unneeded violence to achieve a goal such as overlooking corruption or using non-sec or non-command to engage in ISG-violating behaviour or antagonistic behaviour. - Bargaining is offering reduced punishment or engaging with the terms or demands in a hostage situation if it means reduced harm or the returning of high-value stolen goods.
# SC.4 - Security Captain Clause The Captain should, in most circumstances, not engage with the round as a member of Security. While members of Security may seek advice or training from the Captain, the Captain themself should not seek out antagonists.
However, in the event there are only 2 or less members of Security, excluding Cadets, the Captain may backfill with Security. When doing so, they should endeavour to not utilize their All Access ID in manners that do not comply with the ISG's provisions on entering departments as Security.
A Captain backfilling as Security will be treated as a member of Security OOC when it comes to deciding the threat level of a shift.
[bold]This only applies to Roundstart or Latejoin Captains, not to CO's.[/bold]
# SC.5 - Meta Knowledge While there is no Metashield preventing your character from having knowledge of threats or tools, there is still the expectation that Security engages with Antagonists in an In Character manner.
Your character may know that some members of the crew are seeking to cause trouble, but should not know about the Meta concept of the Troublemaker Antagonist and their kits.
Your character may know about the various spy tools the Syndicate supplies to their agents, but should not assume that these are in play without sufficient in-round evidence.
Do not search PDAs, headsets, or for implants without strong evidence gathered in that round, or if the ISG explicitly instructs you to.
To prevent killing a round, do not confiscate unselected antagonist kits or a thief's unplaced beacon. These items are not considered contraband by themselves. You may treat them as strange storage and a strange fulton beacon, but not as illegal.
